title: Operations governance: checklists and approval flows (company-wide)
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Overview

This document consolidates operational checklists and approval flows used across Redwood Inference for: access & permissions, change management, data management, procurement & expenses, vendor management, travel policies, and internal templates. It is intended as a single-pane reference for requesters, approvers, and operational owners. Keep this page linked from team runbooks and the central policy index.

Scope and applicability

- Applies to all Redwood employees, contractors, and short-term consultants unless a specific policy states otherwise.
- Where teams require stricter controls (e.g., Customer Data or Private deployments), the stricter control overrides these general flows.
- This page summarizes processes and provides links to canonical forms and templates. For legal, security, or major financial commitments, contact finance-legal or security teams directly.

Quick reference: responsible roles

- Requester: individual initiating the request
- Manager: direct manager of the requester; first-line approver for low-to-medium risk/expense requests
- Team Lead / Product Manager: functional owner for product-related changes or vendor use
- Security Owner: security reviewer for access to sensitive systems or production data
- Finance Approver: finance-legal reviewer for procurement and expense commitments beyond thresholds
- Procurement Ops: owns purchase order creation and vendor onboarding checklist

Access & Permissions: summary and checklist

Principles

- Least privilege by default. Grant only the permissions needed to perform the job for the expected duration.
- Time-bound access for contractors and change-window tasks.
- Access revocation must be executed when an employee offboards or role changes.

Types of access and approval flow

1) Standard tooling (Slack, Google Workspace, internal wiki):
   - Request via Self-Serve: use the Access Portal.
   - Approver: Requester’s Manager (auto-approved if manager is also an admin).
   - SLA: 1 business day.

2) Production systems and data (internal services, dashboards, S3 buckets):
   - Request via Access Portal with justification and scoped resource list.
   - Approvers: Manager + Security Owner (must sign off on data sensitivity).
   - Duration: max 90 days for broad roles; contractors maximum 30 days without renewal.
   - SLA: 3 business days.

3) Emergency access (incident response):
   - Request: create incident ticket and tag oncall; security owner provides temporary access via jumpbox or short-lived token.
   - Post-mortem: access must be reviewed within 3 business days and formally documented.

Access checklist (requester)

- Identify resources and exact permissions needed (e.g., read-only, write, admin).
- Provide business justification and expected duration.
- Confirm manager approval via the Access Portal.
- For production/data access, attach data classification and any program-level approvals.

Change management: approval matrix and runbook

Principles

- Changes to production or customer-facing behavior require risk assessment, testing evidence, rollback plan, and staged rollout.
- Non-production infrastructure changes should follow automated CI/CD with peer review.

Change categories and flows

- Minor (low-risk config or non-prod code): peer review + CI green -> deploy via standard pipeline.
  - Approver: Peer reviewer or team lead.
  - Notification: Weekly changelog.

- Major (schema changes, infra scaling, runtime config affecting latency or cost >15%):
  - Approver: Team lead + SRE/Platform reviewer + Product owner.
  - Documentation: RFC or short ADR attached to PR.
  - Rollout: Canary -> regional rollout -> full rollout with metrics gating.

- Security-impacting changes (auth, PKI, encryption config):
  - Approver: Security Owner + Platform Lead.
  - Additional: Pen test or design review required for changes touching customer data.

Change runbook template (must be attached to PR)

1) Summary and purpose
2) Impact analysis (affected services, users, data)
3) Test evidence (unit/integration/e2e results)
4) Rollback steps and expected recovery time (RTO)
5) Monitoring plan and key metrics to watch
6) Communication plan (SLACK channel, customer notices if needed)

Data management: classification and retention checklist

Data classification tiers

- Public: Intended for public consumption. No special controls.
- Internal: Company internal information with no customer PII. Standard access controls.
- Restricted: Customer data, regulated data (PCI/PHI), and any PII. Requires encryption-at-rest, access logging, and stricter onboarding.

Minimum controls by tier

- Public: Regular backups optional, retention per team norms.
- Internal: Encrypted at rest recommended, audit logs enabled for critical datasets. Retention default 12 months unless business case.
- Restricted: Encryption at rest + in transit, KMS-backed keys, RBAC, access reviews quarterly, retention aligned with contract/regulatory obligations.

Retention and deletion flow

- Data owner defines retention in the onboarding form.
- Before disposal, present deletion plan and verification steps to Security Owner.
- For customer data deletion requests, follow the customer-data deletion checklist and log actions against the customer SLA ticket.

Procurement & expenses: thresholds, approvals, templates

Approval thresholds (examples)

| Spend type | Up to | Approver | Notes |
|---|---:|---|---|
| Routine software subscriptions | $5,000 | Manager | Annual renewals allowed with manager approval |
| New vendor contract (software/hardware) | $50,000 | Finance Approver + Procurement Ops | Requires vendor onboarding and PO |
| Capital / multi-year commitments | $250,000 | VP Finance + Legal | Board notice for multi-year strategic commitments |

Procurement checklist (requester)

1) Complete Procurement Request Form (link in templates section).
2) Attach justification, expected term, vendor contact, and security questionnaire if any.
3) Manager approval.
4) Procurement Ops validates vendor, generates PO, and routes to Finance Approver and Legal as needed.

Expense policy highlights

- Use company card for pre-approved travel and team expenses when available.
- Receipts required for all expenses > $25. Exceptions documented and manager-approved.
- Personal expenses on company card are not permitted.

Vendor management and onboarding checklist

- Pre-contract: Security questionnaire (SOC2 summary or security controls), data handling requirements, sanctions check.
- Contract stage: Contract review by Legal + Data Processing Addendum for restricted data.
- Post-signature: Procurement Ops creates vendor record, generates PO, and sets up payment terms.
- Quarterly: Business owner conducts vendor performance review for strategic vendors.

Vendor onboarding checklist (procurement ops)

- Confirm W9 / company tax docs
- Validate bank/payment details via finance procedures
- Configure vendor in AP system and attach contract copy
- Assign vendor owner and expected renewal cadence

Travel and expense policies: quick rules and booking guidance

- Preferred booking channels: Company travel portal or approved travel vendor to ensure rates and travel insurance.
- Pre-approval: Any international travel requires manager + People Ops approval 10 business days in advance.
- Lodging: Standard room, reasonable upgrades require manager approval.
- Per diem: Follow published per diem rates in template.

Travel safety and private deployments site visits

- For private deployment / on-prem customer visits, fill out the Field Visit Risk Assessment and get Security Owner sign off.
- For travel to regions with travel advisories, People Ops will coordinate emergency contact details and insurance coverage.

Internal templates and where to find them

- Procurement Request Form: /confluence/templates/procurement-request-form (use this for all vendor/contract requests).
- Access Request Form: /confluence/templates/access-request
- Change Runbook Template: /confluence/templates/change-runbook
- Travel Approval Form: /confluence/templates/travel-approval
- Vendor Security Questionnaire: /confluence/templates/vendor-security-questionnaire

Operational cadence and reviews

- Quarterly policy review: People Ops + Finance + Security + 1 engineering representative.
- Annual vendor risk assessments for strategic vendors (top 20 by spend).
- Monthly procurement backlog review with Procurement Ops and Finance.

Escalation paths and SLAs

- Access requests: 1 business day for standard tooling; 3 business days for production/data requests.
- Procurement requests: 5 business days for <$50k requests; 15 business days for complex procurements requiring legal.
- Change approvals: minor changes within team SLA; major changes require 3 business days for cross-team review.
